runs.title: Q3 2025 Hiring Funnel — Leadership Pre‑Read
runs.body:
This one-page report summarizes the Q3 2025 hiring funnel and highlights the largest drop-off.

Funnel volume:
- Applications: 1,450
- Interviews: 230
- Offers: 48
- Hires: 35

Conversion and drop-off:
The largest drop-off occurs between Applications and Interviews. From 1,450 applications, 230 progressed to interviews, so 1,220 applicants did not advance at that stage (15.9% interview rate).

Downstream stages show smaller absolute declines. From 230 interviews to 48 offers, 182 fewer candidates moved forward (20.9% offer rate from interview). From 48 offers to 35 hires, 13 offers did not convert to hires, for a 72.9% offer-to-hire conversion rate.

Overall outcome:
Across the full funnel, Q3 resulted in 35 hires from 1,450 applications (2.4% application-to-hire conversion). The data indicates the primary constraint is early-stage screening and selection efficiency, since the majority of candidate attrition occurs prior to interviews.

judge_scores.justification: It accurately reports all funnel counts, clearly emphasizes the largest drop-off (Applications→Interviews) with correct conversions, includes the requested offer-to-hire percentage, and is well-structured and appropriately neutral for leadership, though there is minor repetition of the 72.9% offer-to-hire figure that slightly reduces conciseness.

runs.title: Q3 2025 Hiring Funnel — One-Page Summary
runs.body:
Q3 2025 funnel results show 1,450 applications converting to 35 hires.

Funnel volume by stage
- Applications: 1,450
- Interviews: 230
- Offers: 48
- Hires: 35

Conversion and drop-off highlights
The largest drop-off occurred from Applications to Interviews: 1,450 down to 230, a reduction of 1,220 candidates (230/1,450 = 15.9% progressed). Subsequent stages were less steep: Interviews to Offers declined by 182 (48/230 = 20.9% progressed), and Offers to Hires declined by 13 (35/48 = 72.9% progressed; 72.9% offer-to-hire conversion).

Key takeaway for leadership
The top-of-funnel is providing substantial volume, but screening/selection is the principal constraint. With only 15.9% of applicants reaching interviews, small improvements in application quality, screening efficiency, or criteria clarity would have the largest impact on downstream yield. By contrast, late-stage conversion is comparatively strong: 72.9% offer-to-hire conversion (offer acceptance), resulting in 35 hires.
